clue.text: Maintain quiet reticence

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
reserve is a restrained, reticent manner

explanation.surface: Someone keeping their composure by staying silent and saying little.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it going or keep it intact, which is what maintaining means.

clue.text: Objects to odd pieces

blocks.note: first meaning: aims or goals
second meaning: leftover scraps, as in odds and those

explanation.surface: Someone raising complaints about some leftover bits and bobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' reads as a verb (protests) but is the plural noun meaning purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are aims or purposes, and also leftover fragments, as in the phrase odds and ends.

clue.text: Theologian having to eat about six

indicators.note: the eating word goes about, that is around, the number word

blocks.note: to dine is to eat a meal
six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion sitting down to dinner at around six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a divine is a clergyman or religious scholar, an older usage for an expert in theology.

clue.text: Churchmen of limited mobility as board members?

definitions.text: Churchmen of limited mobility as board members?

blocks.note: surface reading: senior clergy who can't get about much
setter's reading: chess pieces, which may only move diagonally on the board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Board members' suggests directors of a company; here the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: These senior clergy share their name with the chess pieces restricted to diagonal moves on squares of one colour.

clue.text: In the 18th century, a dandy form of pasta

blocks.note: first meaning: a fashionable young man of Georgian England affecting continental style
second meaning: tubular Italian pasta

explanation.surface: A history note: a Georgian fop as a fancy variety of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The dandy sense is the one in 'Yankee Doodle', who stuck a feather in his cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word named showy, over-dressed young men in Georgian times, and also the familiar short tube-shaped Italian noodle.

clue.text: Church done over in rough clay or translucent material

indicators.note: done over means roughed up, so this word's letters are knocked out of order
rough means roughly worked, so the clay word is not in its tidy order

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church rebuilt in rough clay or some glassy semi-transparent substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done over' reads as finished; in slang it means beaten up, a fair signal for a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalcedony is a waxy, semi-transparent quartz mineral, used as a gemstone, so it is a translucent material.

clue.text: Joined the team

blocks.note: first meaning: brought together as one
second meaning: the short name for a football club such as Manchester ...

explanation.surface: A new player signed up with the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British football clubs are called United, and fans call them just that.
explanation.definitionFit: United means combined into one, and is also the everyday name fans use for clubs like Manchester or Leeds.

clue.text: Toast given in port

blocks.note: first meaning: a drinking song or toast, from the Italian
second meaning: a harbour town in the heel of Italy

explanation.surface: Raising a glass of port to propose a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine you might toast with; it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brindisi is a drinking song proposing a toast in opera, and Brindisi is a harbour city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: The short answer without capital?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the short answer goes around the first word

blocks.note: ans. is the usual abbreviation of answer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled request for a brief reply that leaves out the capital letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without capital' seems to mean lower case; 'without' means outside, and 'capital' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Flower that has a duplicate existence

blocks.note: existence as the verb meaning to exist, and duplicate means it appears twice

explanation.surface: A bloom that somehow leads two lives at once.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is a crossword river, something that flows; the Thames is called the Isis at Oxford, so it too has a double life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the stretch of the River Thames through Oxford, and a river is a 'flow-er' in crosswords.

clue.text: One against society as his team lie scattered

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loner opposed to everyone, while his teammates lie strewn about the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Ishmael's hand is 'against every man, and every man's hand against him', so an Ishmaelite is an outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant of Ishmael, whose biblical hand was against everyone, so figuratively an outcast at war with society.

clue.text: Sailors talked about sea voyage

indicators.note: talked about means said out loud, so the sound of the word matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: crews are the sailors manning ships

explanation.surface: Seamen chatting about an ocean trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure trip by ship, which is a voyage at sea.

clue.text: Novelty at pub getting enthusiastic reception

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a burst of applause

explanation.surface: Something new in the local pub that the regulars cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is something newly introduced, a new idea or method, so it is a novelty.

clue.text: Goes on for money

blocks.note: first meaning: continues or advances, as a verb
second meaning: the takings from a sale or event, as a noun

explanation.surface: Someone carrying on purely for the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are stressed differently: pro-CEEDS the verb, PRO-ceeds the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to continue onward, and proceeds are the sum of cash raised by a sale or event.

clue.text: Boy-meets-girl opera

blocks.note: Leo is a boy's name
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A romantic stage work where a boy meets a girl, the standard love-story plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy-meets-girl' is the stock romance formula, but here it is two names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonora was Beethoven's original title for the work later revised as Fidelio, so it names an opera.

clue.text: Persistently irritating foul-smelling fish

blocks.note: rank means having a strong, nasty smell
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A pungent fish that keeps bothering someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rankling keeps causing lingering resentment or annoyance, so it goes on irritating.

clue.text: Understatement used for effect by T.S. Eliot?

indicators.note: the question mark hints that the poet's name is not to be taken at face value but rearranged

blocks.note: the poet's name, initials included

explanation.surface: A literature question: did the poet of The Waste Land favour deliberate understatement?
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms something by denying its opposite, as in 'not bad', a deliberate understatement.

clue.text: Teacher being terribly rude about Roman censor

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly mangled out of its order
the mangled word goes about, around, the name of the Roman

blocks.note: taken as written
Cato the Elder was the famous censor of Rome

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher being very rude about an ancient Roman official.
explanation.walkthrough: A censor in Rome was a magistrate overseeing the census and public morals; Cato the Elder held the post.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is a person whose job is to instruct others, which is what a teacher does.

clue.text: Temper the effects of sausage roll

indicators.note: to roll something tumbles it over, so its letters come out in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sausage roll eaten to ease the after-effects of something, perhaps a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sausage roll' looks like the pastry snack; 'roll' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or lessen something painful, so it moderates its impact.

clue.text: Where sisters study openings?

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
vents are openings or outlets

explanation.surface: A question about where nuns go to examine apertures, or perhaps job openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Convents are the houses in which communities of nuns live, and nuns are called sisters.

clue.text: Equine quadruped - for example roan, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be arranged in some other way

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse-like animal, a roan for instance?
explanation.walkthrough: A roan is a horse with a mixed coat, so it looks like the example of an equine; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is the wild ass of Asia, a four-legged member of the horse family.

clue.text: Lays about churchwomen fleeing for shelter

indicators.note: turned about, so the first word's letters are moved around
fleeing means running back the way they came, so the women's abbreviation goes backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the Mothers' Union, a Church of England women's organisation

explanation.surface: Songs about women of the church running off to find refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mothers' Union (MU) is a Christian women's charity in the Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a place of refuge or protection, such as sanctuary given to those fleeing danger.

clue.text: Sour beer  - one sort of lager, perhaps?

indicators.note: sort of suggests a variant version of the beer word, with its letters rearranged

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a soured ale might count as one kind of lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegar is malt vinegar, literally soured ale, so it is ale that has turned acid.

clue.text: Is unable to press ale out of melon?

indicators.note: read with the word before it as out of order, so the letters are knocked into a new sequence

blocks.note: can't means is unable, apostrophe dropped
p is a short form of press, as in the press
taken as written
the word less its final T, which the opening block has already supplied

explanation.surface: Can't squeeze the beer from a melon, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: OU, needed for the shuffle, has to come from the 'out' of 'out of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a variety of musk melon with orange flesh and a ribbed rind.

clue.text: Catch some on return

indicators.note: on return means coming back the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Catching a few things as they come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device for capturing animals, and to trap is to catch.

clue.text: Time for some great idea

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: It is high time for a good brainwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide is an old word for a time or season, still seen in Eastertide and Yuletide.

clue.text: Leading lady deprived of oriental drug

indicators.note: deprived of means losing something, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: the heroine is the female lead of a story
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: A star actress stripped of her eastern narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are pronounced the same, which makes the clue's link especially neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin is a highly addictive opiate narcotic made from morphine, a notorious illegal drug.

clue.text: Great issue, relatively speaking

blocks.note: grand means great
a son is issue, an offspring

explanation.surface: A major problem, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem, and 'relatively' like 'comparatively'; here they mean offspring and family relations.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a child's child, descendant one generation further down, the 'great' offspring in family terms.
